B) HOLD BOTH THE RESPONDENTS JOINTLY AND SEVERALLY LIABLE TO PAY THE ENHANCED COMPENSATION TO THE APPELLANT.
THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,

THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

The appellant is in appeal challenging the quantum of compensation awarded by the Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Chittapur in MVC No.284/2021.
2.
The appellant is a head constable in the department of police, who suffered injuries in a road traffic accident that occurred on 20.05.2020.

Due to the accident, the appellant suffered the following injuries:
1. Abrasion over the left hand and left thigh.

2. Swelling and deformity on left thigh 3. Fracture of left femur.
4. Swelling of left hand.
5. Fracture of middle and distal phalanx of left little finger.
3.

On a claim petition filed by the appellant under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, the Tribunal awarded the following compensation :
1. Pain and Agony Rs.50,000-00 2.

Medical Expenses Rs.1,83,181-00 3. Loss of amenities and Rs.30,000-00 nutritious food 4. Loss of income during laid Rs.50,000-00 up period TOTAL Rs.3,13,181-00 the same is rounded off to Rs.3,13,200-00 Being aggrieved by the quantum of compensation, the appellant is before this Court.

4. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the injuries were serious in nature and therefore,
the compensation awarded towards pain and suffering undergone by the appellant was meager.
In addition, he also submits that the compensation awarded towards loss of amenities due to the injuries is inadequate.
He further submits that the attendant charges is also not awarded by the Tribunal.

5. Learned counsel for the Insurance Company on the other hand submits that the Tribunal has ordered reimbursement of medical expenses, though the appellant was a police head constable and was entitled for reimbursement of medical expenses.

She further submits that the appellant was awarded loss of income during laid up period though the appellant did not produce any material to show that he had suffered loss of income during laid up period.
Therefore, she submits that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper and does not require any enhancement.
6. I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the appellant as well as the learned counsel for respondent No.2.

7. Though the learned counsel for respondent No.2 contended that the Tribunal has awarded compensation towards reimbursement of medical expenses and loss of income during laid up period, it is unfortunate that the insurer has not filed any appeal challenging the award passed by the Tribunal.

The impugned judgment discloses that the Tribunal did not award adequate compensation towards attendant charges and therefore, this Court considers it appropriate to enhance the compensation from Rs.3,13,200/- to a sum of Rs.3,50,000/-.
8.
In view of the above, the appeal is allowed in part and the compensation determined by the Tribunal is enhanced to Rs.3,50,000/-.
The enhanced compensation of Rs.36,800/- shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realization.
The insurer shall deposit the enhanced compensation of Rs.36,800/- along with interest before the Tribunal within one month from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.
